domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
attributes: reversesRequestId: string | null (NEW — null for every ordinary request; non-null only on a reversal row)
domain_entities.purpose: The canonical leave-request aggregate. Under GP-008 an APPROVED instance is a completed approval and becomes immutable; cancellation of an APPROVED request is expressed by a separate LeaveRequestReversal row rather than by mutating this one.

domain_entities.name: LeaveRequestReversal
attributes: reversesRequestId: string (non-null — the original APPROVED request id)
requestedDays: number (copied from original, never re-derived)
domain_entities.purpose: The new LeaveRequest row created when an APPROVED request is cancelled. It is a distinct domain role of LeaveRequest: a faithful snapshot of the original that is born in CANCELLED and points back at the original via reversesRequestId. It exists so the completed approval (the original APPROVED row) is never modified.

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: The per-employee, per-leave-type, per-accrual-period reservation ledger. Unchanged by this feature except that the release triggered by an approved cancellation must still happen exactly once, in the same unit of work as the reversal insert.

domain_entities.name: AuditLog
domain_entities.purpose: Immutable audit record (GP-002). The cancellation of an APPROVED request still writes exactly one CANCEL record inside the same unit of work as the reversal insert and the balance release.

domain_entities.name: LeaveRequestView
attributes: reversesRequestId: string | null (NEW — exposed on the wire)
domain_entities.purpose: The read-model projection returned by GET /leaves and GET /leaves/:id. Because a cancelled-after-approval request is now two rows, the projection must expose reversesRequestId so a client can tell the original APPROVED row from the reversal CANCELLED row.

business_rules: GP-008 immutability: once a LeaveRequest reaches APPROVED (a completed approval), its status, approverId, approvalComment and decidedAt are immutable. No operation may update those fields on an APPROVED row. Cancellation of an APPROVED request must not write to the original row at all. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest completed-approval immutability (all operations that could touch an APPROVED row) appears, not only here]

Reversal creates a NEW instance: cancelling an APPROVED request inserts a new LeaveRequest row with status CANCELLED and reversesRequestId = the original request id. The original APPROVED row is left byte-identical. The reversal row is born in CANCELLED and never transitions again. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequestReversal creation (approved-cancellation path) appears, not only here]

In-place cancellation is preserved for non-completed states: cancelling a DRAFT or SUBMITTED request mutates that same row to CANCELLED (with cancelledBy/cancelledAt) exactly as today. No completed approval exists in those states, so GP-008 does not apply and no reversal row is created. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest cancellation (DRAFT/SUBMITTED path) appears, not only here]

Balance release on approved cancellation is exactly-once and unchanged in amount: the original request's requestedDays is returned to usedDays (usedDays -= requestedDays, no pro-rating) exactly once, inside the same unit of work as the reversal insert. The release must not be skipped and must not be applied twice (e.g. it must not be triggered by both the original row and the reversal row). [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalance release semantics for cancellation appears, not only here]

requestedDays = endDate - startDate + 1 (inclusive calendar days, whole-day UTC, no weekend/holiday exclusion) is the single canonical day-count derivation, computed once via the shared requestedDays helper. The reversal row copies the original's requestedDays verbatim and never re-derives it; the balance release consumes that same copied value. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever requestedDays day-count derivation (all consumers: sufficiency check, reservation, release, reversal copy) appears, not only here]

The cancellation of an APPROVED request still writes exactly one AuditLog record with action CANCEL, entityType 'leave_request', entityId = the reversal row id, beforeState = the original APPROVED request, afterState = the reversal row — inside the same unit of work as the reversal insert and the balance release (GP-002).

Wire honesty: because a cancelled-after-approval request is represented by two rows, the read model (GET /leaves, GET /leaves/:id) must expose reversesRequestId so a client can distinguish the original APPROVED row (reversesRequestId = null) from the reversal CANCELLED row (reversesRequestId = original id). A client must never have to infer the pairing from matching dates or employeeId. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequestView read projection appears, not only here]

Authorization and timing guards for cancellation are unchanged by this feature: the owner may cancel their own DRAFT/SUBMITTED request; only the direct manager or an ADMIN may cancel an APPROVED request; cancellation is blocked once startDate <= today (UTC day comparison) with ConflictError. The reversal row inherits the original's employeeId, so role-scoped visibility (EMPLOYEE self, MANAGER self + direct reports, ADMIN all) applies to it identically. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest cancellation authorization and visibility appears, not only here]

A reversal row is terminal and inert: it reserves nothing (no pendingDays/usedDays effect of its own), cannot be submitted, approved, rejected or cancelled again, and is never the target of a second reversal. Only the original APPROVED row's requestedDays drives the single balance release. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequestReversal terminal semantics appears, not only here]
domain_notes:
Lifecycle states introduced or newly load-bearing by this feature (for architectureMdUpdate):

- LeaveRequest: DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED (unchanged set). New binding semantics: APPROVED is a TERMINAL, IMMUTABLE state (GP-008) — status/approverId/approvalComment/decidedAt may never be updated once APPROVED. DRAFT and SUBMITTED remain mutable and are cancelled in place.
- LeaveRequestReversal: CANCELLED (single state; the row is born CANCELLED and never transitions). This is a new domain role of LeaveRequest, not a new table concept — it is a LeaveRequest row with reversesRequestId non-null. It is terminal and inert: no submit/approve/reject/cancel, no reservation, never itself reversed.
- LeaveBalance: OPEN, CLOSED (unchanged). Cancellation of an APPROVED request releases requestedDays from usedDays exactly once, in the same unit of work as the reversal insert.
- AuditLog: RECORDED (unchanged). One CANCEL record per approved cancellation, written in the same unit of work.
- LeaveRequestView: no lifecycle (immutable read projection); gains reversesRequestId on the wire.

Named transitions (all documented above as businessRules):
- cancelInPlace: DRAFT -> CANCELLED and SUBMITTED -> CANCELLED (mutates the same row; SUBMITTED also releases pendingDays).
- reverseApproved: APPROVED -> (original row unchanged) + new LeaveRequestReversal row in CANCELLED with reversesRequestId = original id; releases usedDays on the balance; writes CANCEL audit; notifies requester.

Cross-entity rules that cross boundaries: the reversal row and the balance release and the audit record are one atomic unit of work; the release amount is the original's requestedDays (canonical inclusive day count, copied not re-derived); role-scoped visibility applies to the reversal row via its inherited employeeId.

Open questions recorded: CANCEL audit entityId target (reversal vs original); whether the reversal row copies approval provenance or leaves it null; whether GET /leaves returns both rows or collapses them.

open_questions.question: For the CANCEL audit record written when an APPROVED request is reversed, should entityId be the new reversal row's id or the original APPROVED request's id?
open_questions.impact: Determines how an auditor reconstructs the cancellation from audit_logs alone. If entityId is the reversal id, the audit trail for the original APPROVED request shows no CANCEL entry and the pairing must be recovered via reversesRequestId; if it is the original id, the original's audit history reads as a mutation even though the row was never mutated.
candidate_options: entityId = reversal row id, beforeState = original APPROVED request, afterState = reversal row (audit follows the new instance)
entityId = original APPROVED request id, beforeState = original, afterState = reversal row (audit follows the reversed instance)
Write two records: one against the original (referencing the reversal) and one against the reversal

open_questions.question: Should the reversal row preserve the original's approval provenance (approverId, approvalComment, decidedAt) as copied values, or leave them null?
open_questions.impact: Affects whether a client reading only the reversal row can see who approved the leave that was later reversed, and whether the reversal row could be mistaken for a request that was never approved. Copying them risks implying the reversal itself was approved; nulling them loses provenance unless the client follows reversesRequestId.
candidate_options: Null on the reversal row; provenance is reached by following reversesRequestId to the immutable original
Copy approverId/approvalComment/decidedAt verbatim onto the reversal row as a snapshot
Copy decidedAt only (the approval instant) and null approverId/approvalComment

open_questions.question: Should GET /leaves return both the original APPROVED row and its reversal CANCELLED row as two list entries, or collapse them into one logical entry?
open_questions.impact: Determines list length, pagination counts, and whether a client sees a leave that is simultaneously APPROVED and CANCELLED. The feature requires the client be able to tell the rows apart, which presumes both are returned, but the list contract itself is not stated.
candidate_options: Return both rows unchanged; the client pairs them via reversesRequestId
Return both rows but annotate the original as reversed (e.g. a derived reversedByRequestId)
Return only the reversal row and suppress the original from the list
